1: # AGENTS.md — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City
2: 
3: How to behave in this repo. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Words and the path index are `docs/project/ref-glossary.md`. Decisions are `docs/adr/`. Conventions for `docs/project/` — prefixes, document size, one fact one home — are `docs/project/index.md`.
4: 
5: Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.
6: 
7: A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; do not copy a row here. `docs/specs/` is a rule that is still true. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. `build/` and `scratchpad/` are disposable and never cited. A name says when to open the file: a date means a record, `law-` means a procedure read before that kind of work.
8: 
9: When a ticket or workstream ends, distill its durable findings into `docs/project/`. A finding is admitted only as a measured fact, a repeatable procedure, or a named pitfall — never a narrative, a chronology, or a status. One fact, one home.
10: 
11: ## Product
12: 
13: Sandbox-City (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 千星奇域 map — free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger — driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN Sandbox-City; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1–S6 and wiring M1–M7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.
14: 
15: The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.
16: 
17: ## Stack
18: 
19: Genshin Impact 千星奇域 UGC; the editor is 千星沙箱, PC-only (`PRD.md` § Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.
20: 
21: Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.
22: 
23: `platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter — local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.
24: 
25: A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.
26: 
27: ## Contracts
28: 
29: - A surface's state machine owns phase and outcomes. The control layer only displays them. Logic inside a draw path is a defect.
30: - Settlement is event-driven. Mora changes on the settle event, never on a clock. Exactly one write seam (`PRD.md` F13, M2).
31: - Rewrite control text when the fact changes. Never rebuild a surface to change one number.
32: - Fragile areas — report, do not fix. A change names the invariant: the Mora ledger write (never negative, re-granted at stage start, forfeit on leave) and its save-key namespace; the phase owner (`PRD.md` M1); the structure, enemy, enhancement and stage tables in `PRD.md` § Content of record; the placement-capacity rule (`PRD.md` F4) — eight placed structures including the Command Base.
33: 
34: ## Localization
35: 
36: EN and CN are co-equal, authored together. No player-facing literal in code or in an editor text field. Both entries of a key land in the same change. Parity is opening `locale/en.lua` and `locale/zh_cn.lua`. Never import the source game's locale files. Do not quote a remembered key total.
37: 
38: ## Verification
39: 
40: The legibility gate (`PRD.md` NFR12) is a human judgement. An agent cannot pass it. Capture is a pre-check, never acceptance. Where you cannot play, say the requirement is unverified. Graceful degradation is `PRD.md` NFR18; the game plays with motion off (NFR13).
41: 
42: ## Issues and decisions
43: 
44: File a defect with a failing check under `issue-tracker/open/` before the fix. Do not file a doc or process issue. Do not write a handover file. Numbering and moves: `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md`. An issue file is never deleted.
45: 
46: ADRs are product and content decisions, written before the decision is implemented. Workplace rules are not ADRs. Convention: `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md`. The live list is `docs/adr/index.md`.
47: 
48: `archive/` is proof, never required reading. Do not edit it and do not append inside it.
49: 
50: ## Editing
51: 
52: No bulk replace and no tree-wide regex: both have corrupted UTF-8 and CN strings (千星奇域, 千星沙箱, 摩拉). After a multi-file edit, confirm each file still decodes as UTF-8.
53: 
54: Cite paths relative to the repo root. The one sibling path allowed is `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`. A machine-local absolute needs `<!-- device-path: … -->` on that same block. `file:///` is never used.
55: 
56: One writer per file. A non-owner writes the exact wording into the owning ticket. One git writer per checkout; concurrent lanes may use separate worktrees. Commits are pathspec-limited. No history surgery in a shared checkout.
57: 
58: ## Shell and the game
59: 
60: Every shell command has a positive timeout and does only what was asked. Never a watcher, dev server, REPL, or open-ended job. No CI, and do not add one.
61: 
62: Never kill the game process. Exit a playtest in-game: Esc, then 中断挑战, then 离开. Force-kill `YuanShen.exe` only when the game is frozen and that path does not work.
63: 
64: Publishing a map is a human action. Never submit or publish through the Sandbox, and never touch a published map. Push, PRs, tags, and write-scoped `gh` only when the human asks in this conversation.
65: 
66: From the Genshin main menu: Esc, scroll to the bottom, 我的奇域. Esc on an editor tab returns to the editor menu; Esc again toggles the left bar. The third button on that bar is the save-file manager. Turn logging on every time the editor opens, or the session writes no `.gia`: 千星沙箱 window, 窗口 → 日志, scroll 选择单位 to the bottom, tick 客户端脚本. Further click-paths are `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md`, and only during a Sandbox session.
67: 
68: ## Standing rules
69: 1. Summon subagents in background mode by default.
70: 2. Owner works from 2 devices: one has `C:\Users\AAAAA\`, the other has `C:\Users\TZ\`.
71: 3. Never invent jargon, codenames, or project shorthand. Talk to the human in plain, very concise language, as if he has ADHD: short sentences, concrete words, no metaphors, no private vocabulary. A term that needs explaining to a newcomer is not allowed in a sentence to the owner.
72: 4. Run the smallest test set that can fail. Do not run end-to-end tests when unit tests cover the change. Group tests into one run instead of starting one run per change.

(End of file - total 72 lines)

1: # project — the project documentation index
2: 
3: Always read this index on entering `docs/project/`. It is the index for this repo; no second overview file sits beside it.
4: 
5: ## Routing
6: 
7: | Kind of thing | Home |
8: | --- | --- |
9: | A measured platform fact | one row in `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` |
10: | How to build | `docs/project/building/` |
11: | A rule that is still true | `docs/specs/` (entry list: `docs/specs/index.md`; proposed game-repo patterns are labelled there and in each file) |
12: | Operating the editor or the game | `docs/project/sessions/` |
13: | A rule for working on this repo | `docs/guides/` |
14: | A product or content decision | `docs/adr/` |
15: | In-flight work | `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` until its results are written up or archived |
16: | A raw record | `archive/` — written once, never required reading |
17: 
18: ## Naming and chunking
19: 
20: Three prefixes, on files and on index lines. `law-` is binding: read it before doing the kind of work the filename names. `ref-` is reference: open it only when the task touches the named topic, and it is the default for project knowledge. `work-` is in-flight notes for one effort: a law or ref file never cites it, and it is written up or archived when the effort ends. This file is the statement of those conventions.
21: 
22: A chunk is one concern, stands alone, and opens with one scope line naming its section. Its body caps at 250 lines; past that it splits by concern, never by part number, and the split updates this directory's index in the same change. Each fact lives in one place; other chunks link to it. English and its Chinese twin stay inside the same concern chunk.
23:

1: # CONTEXT — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City
2: 
3: Glossary and path index. Rules live in `AGENTS.md`. Product truth is `PRD.md`. Decisions live in `docs/adr/`.
4: 
5: ## Glossary
6: 
7: ### Platform
8: 
9: - **Miliastra Wonderland** (千星奇域): Genshin's official UGC platform — players enter published maps, creators author them. Avoid: Genshin UGC mode, the Roblox thing.
10: - **Miliastra Sandbox** (千星沙箱): the PC-only authoring editor; it holds the platform's two places to write game logic — the node graph (the half that runs on the server) and client controls with Lua client scripts. Avoid: the editor, the sandbox (unqualified), "the scripting language" for the client half.
11: - **Client control**: a 2D UI element authored in the Sandbox and driven at runtime by a Lua client script — image, text, deck selector, UI effect, container. A control renders code-owned gameplay sprite data. Avoid: UI element, widget, node, sprite (the art data shown, never the control showing it).
12: - **Platform-free core** (可移植核心): the pure-Lua rules region in `platform-free-core/` — it names no client control, no save variable and no platform call. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. Avoid: engine, framework, backend, library.
13: - **Cloud-save variable**: the platform's only persistence — no filesystem, no OS save file (`PRD.md`). Avoid: save file, state.json, local storage.
14: - **Sprite** (精灵图): code-owned gameplay art data rendered through a client control, never an externally uploaded or imported gameplay image (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay. Avoid: asset pipeline, texture, atlas, resource, drawable.
15: 
16: ### Scope
17: 
18: - **Source game** (Enigmata: Stellar War): the Flash open-field tower defense this project re-expresses; held read-only as `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/`, mechanics re-typed, never ported as-is. Avoid: the origin repo (there is none — the origin is a reference set, not a sibling repo), the decompile (that is one file set inside it).
19: 
20: ### Economy and round
21: 
22: - **Mora** (摩拉): the one economy token — a single currency, no premium or gacha path, earned and spent only inside a run; every movement routes through the one ledger seam (`PRD.md` M2, F13). Avoid: wallet, Stargem (another project's token), credit.
23: - **Wave**: one timed enemy assault between build phases — the round unit. Avoid: round (unqualified), level, stage (that names the campaign unit).
24: 
25: ### Content
26: 
27: - **Command Base**: the player's own structure in the field — enemies fire on it, and its loss is the loss condition (`PRD.md` F12); never purchasable and never sold (`PRD.md` F6). It counts toward the placement cap of eight (`PRD.md` F4). Avoid: base (unqualified), home, nexus.
28: - **Structure**: a defensive piece the player places on the open field. The Command Base is a structure; the rest of the roster is purchasable (`PRD.md` F6). Avoid: tower (unqualified), building, unit.
29: 
30: ### Presentation
31: 
32: - **Legibility gate**: the decisive human acceptance test for every legibility-critical surface — a face identified correctly at normal play distance by someone who did not build it; a pass/fail test an agent can never pass (`PRD.md` NFR12). Avoid: readability check, visual QA.
33: 
34: ## Index
35: 
36: | When | File | One line |
37: | --- | --- | --- |
38: | Product truth, surfaces, requirements | `PRD.md` | Requirements, grouped by screen (S1–S6) and by wiring piece (M1–M7). |
39: | Which decision is live | `docs/adr/index.md` | One row per ADR; the Law cell copies the record's one-sentence decision. |
40: | Writing or amending an ADR | `docs/guides/law-writing-an-adr.md` | Numbering, the parts of an ADR file, and how to write its index row. |
41: | Filing or moving an issue | `docs/guides/law-editing-issue-files.md` | Numbering, moves, and tracker protection. |
42: | A module in `platform-free-core/` | `platform-free-core/README.md` | What such a module may name, and how the allowed Lua subset is enforced. |
43: | Whether a construct is allowed | `docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md` | The Lua 5.1-safe subset that the static check enforces. |
44: | A gameplay sprite's data shape or control cost | `docs/project/building/ref-sprite-rect-encoding.md` | How `tools/sprite_encode/` describes a sprite as rectangles, and how it counts the controls a sprite costs. |
45: | A Sandbox session | `docs/project/sessions/law-editor-sessions.md` | The exact editor clicks; only during a Sandbox session. |
46: | An engine figure or cap | `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` | Engine measurements live there; a number copied into this repo is stale. |
47: | The source game's mechanics | `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/00-index.md` | Inventory and scope of the read-only Enigmata: Stellar War set. |
48: | A player-facing string | `locale/en.lua`, `locale/zh_cn.lua` | Both locales; count the keys in the files. |

1: # PRD — Taskworld Project · Sandbox-City
2: 
3: This file is product truth: every id cited elsewhere — surfaces, requirements, NFRs, posture rows, standing rules, open decisions — resolves here.
4: 
5: ## 1. Product statement
6: 
7: The player defends one open field: they place a handful of structures with their own hand, watch a timed enemy wave come at them, spend the Mora those kills returned on the next structure or the next upgrade, and finish the stage against a boss — in one sitting, on PC, alone. It is a 千星奇域 (Miliastra Wonderland) map driven by Lua client scripts and editor-authored client controls; its code name is `Taskworld-Project` (internal, never player-facing). What makes it worth playing is how much is forced into a few choices: eight placements and one currency force a real decision every intermission, and the five-stage campaign teaches that decision rather than rationing it out. The content set of record is the reduced set of section 7: 8 structures, 18 enemies, 5 stages, 12 enhancements, 6 talents, 8 items, 7 achievements.
8: 
9: ## 2. Platform
10: 
11: The stack, editor constraints and platform caveats live in `AGENTS.md` (Stack and platform); this document designs inside 5.1's constraints and waits on 5.2's assumptions.
12: 
13: ## 3. Goals and non-goals
14: 
15: ### 3.1 Goals
16: 
17: A goal is what a good session looks like; each is checkable by playing, and each is measured by the rows named beside it.
18: 
19: | # | Goal | Measured by |
20: | --- | --- | --- |
21: | G1 | A stranger clears Stage 1 on their first attempt and understands why if they lose. | F5, F12, F23, F29 |
22: | G2 | Every Mora movement is visible as a fact the moment it happens — the player can always say what they can afford. | F13-F21, NFR6, NFR7 |
23: | G3 | The build decision differs per stage: the roster, capacity and unlock chain force a different field each time. | F4-F11, F34 |
24: | G4 | A boss stage reads as a distinct fight — the phase flip is legible and winnable with prep, not with twitch. | F28, F9, F31 |
25: | G5 | Progress outlives the session: stages, stars, talents and achievements read back on the next visit, or degrade honestly. | F35-F39, NFR16 |
26: 
27: ### 3.2 Non-goals
28: 
29: Named so nobody helpfully adds them later; each is out of scope for v1 with its reason.
30: 
31: - No multiplayer, no co-op, no shared stake: no server authority exists to arbitrate one, and the stake of a run is the player's own (R3, D3).
32: - No premium currency, no gacha, no purchase path, no payout of any kind (pillar 3, N1, N2).
33: - No tile grid, no maze-building constraint, no terrain cost: the field is continuous and open (`other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/02_MAP_AND_BUILDING.md`); a grid would be a different game.
34: - No external gameplay image upload/import path and no text-canvas composition; gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (N5, D2).
35: - No ported Flash code, no genshin-ts/TypeScript pipeline, no node-graph logic for v1 mechanics: the code examples in the seed corpus (the previous attempt's design documents) are read with that caveat; logic is re-typed as Lua client scripts.
36: - No endless mode, no difficulty tiers beyond the recorded Normal pacing, no stage 6: out of scope, and only a human decision adds them.
37: - No persistence of in-stage state — balance, placed structures, wave index: a stage is a transaction (F39).
38: - No audio, fonts or 3D model content in v1 (N4, D1): the game must be fully playable silent (NFR13, NFR14).
39: - No mobile authoring or mobile acceptance target: the editor is PC-only (5.1); play on mobile is a look.
40: 
41: ## 4. Product pillars
42: 
43: The small set of promises every design decision is checked against.
44: 
45: 1. Readable command — the field reads as facts, not as motion. If a player cannot tell phase, balance, wave and threat apart at a glance, the surface is re-scoped, not animated harder.
46: 2. One economy, one owner — the Mora (摩拉) ledger is one number changed by named events at one seam (F13); no display path, timer or animation may mint or burn it (NFR6, NFR10).
47: 3. Economy posture — no real-money or platform-currency path anywhere: cosmetic-only stakes, no purchase path, no payout of any kind. Weaken it only by a human decision recorded in its own N row and, if it changes architecture, its own ADR.
48: 
49: ## 5. Platform constraints
50: 
51: ### 5.1 What the build must live inside
52: 
53: | Constraint | Consequence for this product |
54: | --- | --- |
55: | Logic is Lua client scripts, driving client controls authored in the editor. | The whole game is scripts plus control layouts. No engine, no framework, no build step, no platform libraries or vendor modules at runtime: a facility the runtime does not supply is rewritten in portable Lua (`AGENTS.md`, Stack and platform). |
56: | Client-local and server-side are separate domains. | Single-player logic may sit client-local; anything whose outcome must match for all players lives in a server-side graph. Nothing shared-stake is designed before the multiplayer decision (R3, D3). |
57: | The simultaneous-visible-control budget is the binding constraint. | All surfaces share one visible-control budget; hiding a whole group is the only relief valve, and whether a script may do it is A7. If it may not, the split-map fallback (section 8.3) is the plan, not an emergency. |
58: | Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls. | No external gameplay image upload/import path exists. The measured sprite-data and control capacity lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`; design against it. Cover imagery is outside gameplay. |
59: | Persistence is cloud-save variables only. No filesystem, no file I/O; whether `require` spans files is unresolved. | Persistent state is a variable with a capacity budget; a key registry with version stamps is needed before the first key is written (NFR16); save scope is A8. |
60: | Caps are documented, unit-less and scope-unconfirmed; the editor is PC-only. | Every printed cap digit is documentation, never a designable number — each is an early verification task (5.2), and layouts are designed against confirmed answers only. Playtesting on mobile is a look, not an edit. |
61: 
62: ### 5.2 Platform facts and open questions
63: 
64: What the device has actually measured — layout, the tick, per-control text, runtime control creation, the caps and the sprite budget — lives in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`, and what remains unknown — cross-session save, group show/hide, cloud-save scope — is kept as open questions in `docs/project/platform/ref-platform-facts.md`. Design against the measured rows in ENGINE.md; the open questions have one `Type: research` issue each, and each resolves into an ADR where the answer changes architecture. The earlier practice of treating these as assumptions to be gated is retired (see `AGENTS.md`, Platform facts and open questions).
65: 
66: ## 6. Functional requirements
67: 
68: The acceptance column is a human instruction, not a test: a person can pass or fail the row in 千星沙箱 by doing what the row says, on the row's surface, with no tooling attached. What an agent may verify is narrow — arithmetic, wave ordering, AI policy and economy totals, executed in `platform-free-core/` under the local interpreter; no agent may claim that a screen reads, that a face is legible, that a layout fits, that a control budget held, or that persistence worked across a real session (`AGENTS.md`, Visual verification). Requirement IDs are append-only: a withdrawn item keeps its number.
69: 
70: ID conventions: bare, dot-free identifiers, each in one registry — F functional requirement (6.1); G goal (3.1); N product posture row (6.5); NFR non-functional requirement (6.4); R standing rule (6.6); A platform assumption (5.2); D open product decision (6.7); S surface (6.2); M wiring piece (6.3). IDs are never reused for a different meaning.
71: 
72: ### 6.1 Requirements F1-F40
73: 
74: Placement and the field.
75: 
76: | # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |
77: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
78: | F1 | S3 | Structures may be placed at any authored buildable position of the open field; the position is continuous, not snapped to a grid. | Place two turrets at visibly different, non-grid-aligned points; both stay where set for the rest of the stage. |
79: | F2 | S3 | Placement is a two-tap act: choose a structure type, then designate a field position; a cancel path returns to the roster without spending. | Tap-cancel after selecting but before designating: balance unchanged, no structure on the field. |
80: | F3 | S3 | Placement and sell-back are accepted only in the PREP/BUILD phase. | Attempt both during COMBAT: refused, with the reason shown, and the balance unchanged. |
81: | F4 | S2 | Placement capacity: at most 8 placed structures including the Command Base (Content of record), raisable only by the recorded capacity enhancement (F18). | Fill to capacity, attempt one more: refused with the capacity reason; capacity reads 8/8 before the attempt. |
82: | F5 | S3 | Every refusal names its reason from a closed set — capacity, insufficient Mora, outside the build zone, position occupied — as a keyed string in both locales. | Trigger all four refusals in one stage; four different messages, none blank, none a raw key. |
83: | F6 | S3 | The buildable roster is exactly the seven buildable structure types of Content of record at their recorded costs, HP, damage, fire interval and range; the Command Base is authored into the field and never purchasable. | Open the roster: seven entries, each showing the recorded cost; the Command Base is absent from it and present on the field. |
84: | F7 | S2 | Each structure fights by its recorded table row — single target, pierce (2), splash with burn (3), slow (4), homing volley (7) — with no per-frame recomputation of authored data. | Watch one wave pass a mixed line; each tower's visible effect matches its row (splash hits more than one, the ray slows, the blaster pierces armor). |
85: | F8 | S2 | Flying enemies (Content of record, types 130-132) may be engaged only by the anti-air set 1, 2 and 7. | Bring a flying wave against a line with no anti-air: nothing engages the flyers; add one Arcane Turret and it does. |
86: | F9 | S2 | Mora Vault accrues Mora on the economy accrual beat (Content of record) at the recorded rate, at most 3 vaults active, and only while the phase is COMBAT or BOSS. | Two stages, one with 3 vaults one with none: the vaulted balance climbs during combat and is flat during PREP/BUILD and after the last wave. |
87: | F10 | S2 | Ward Barrier blocks ground pathing and takes fire in place of what is behind it, and grants the recorded resistance to adjacent structures; flyers ignore it entirely. | Ground waves stall at the barrier and chew it instead of the towers behind it; a flyer flies straight past the same barrier. |
88: | F11 | S3 | Magic Missile Array is purchasable only after Stage 3 is cleared. | Locked in S1-S3 with the reason shown; present and buyable in S4. |
89: | F12 | S2 | The Command Base holds the recorded HP, cannot be sold, relocated or repaired by spend, and its destruction ends the stage in defeat at once. | Let a wave through with no defenses: the run ends the moment the base falls, and the results surface says why. |
90: 
91: The Mora economy.
92: 
93: | # | [M] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |
94: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
95: | F13 | M2 | Exactly one place changes the Mora balance — the ledger seam M2. Every source and sink in this section routes through it and nowhere else. | Play a full stage and read the balance history: every movement is one of the named events in F14; there is no unexplained drift. |
96: | F14 | M2 | The ledger's sources are: kill reward (F19), vault accrual (F9), item pickup (F32), stage-clear bonus (F20), achievement reward (F37), sell-back (F17). Its sinks are: structure purchase (F6), enhancement purchase (F18), talent activation (F31). Nothing else mints or burns Mora. | Enumerate a session's movements against that list; no seventh source and no fourth sink appears. |
97: | F15 | M2 | The balance is never negative and never fractional: a purchase whose cost exceeds the balance is refused before the seam, and every credit is an integer. | Spam-buy the most expensive item until refused; the balance stops at 0 or the remainder and never reads below zero. |
98: | F16 | M2 | A stage always begins by granting its recorded starting Mora (Content of record) — a fresh session, a retry and a return from the hub all re-grant it. No balance is ever read out of persistence. | Start, abandon and restart Stage 3: the opening balance is the recorded figure each time, never a stale one. |
99: | F17 | M2 | Sell-back returns 50% of that structure's purchase cost, integer-divided (rounded down), in PREP/BUILD only; enhancement spend on a sold structure is not refunded. | Sell a 350-cost mortar: +175; sell one that carried enhancement spend and the enhancement cost stays spent. |
100: | F18 | M2 | Enhancements: 12 rows in 6 categories (Content of record), purchasable only in PREP/BUILD and INTERMISSION. Cost of level n = `baseCost + costScale × (n − 1)`; each category caps at its recorded level; effects apply as computed multipliers over authored base stats, never by mutating authored data. Capacity extension raises F4's cap by the recorded amount per level. | Buy the same enhancement to its cap and stop: the button reads capped; the tower's damage recomputes from base × recorded per-level factor. |
101: | F19 | M2 | Kill reward pays on the kill event, at the recorded figure for that enemy, adjusted only by the recorded rank and economy multipliers, integer. | Clear a wave twice with the same seeded order: identical totals; adding Mora Amplifier raises the total by its recorded factor and nothing else changes. |
102: | F20 | M2 | The stage-clear bonus follows the ratified figure set of Content of record and is paid on the VICTORY event. Intermission pays no bonus at all. | Clear Stage 1: the results readout shows the recorded bonus; between waves 1 and 2 the balance moves only from kills and vaults. |
103: | F21 | M2 | The in-stage ledger is session-scoped: nothing about it — balance, purchases, earned rank — travels to the next stage or the next visit. | Clear S1 rich, open S2: the opening balance is S2's grant, not S1's remainder. |
104: 
105: Phases, waves and combat.
106: 
107: | # | [M] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |
108: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
109: | F22 | M5 | The field never holds more enemies at once than the authored wave names: overflow waits in the spawn queue and is never dropped, and nothing but the scheduler creates an enemy. | Push a large wave through one narrow line: every enemy the wave list names eventually appears, none is missing when the wave ends, and the on-field count never exceeds the authored concurrency. |
110: | F23 | M1 | One phase owner drives the six-phase state machine: LOBBY/READY → PREP/BUILD → COMBAT → INTERMISSION → (PREP/BUILD ∣ BOSS) → VICTORY ∣ DEFEAT. No surface advances state on its own timer, and no transition happens without its named event. | Watch the phase readout through a whole stage: it never skips, never re-enters a phase out of order, and every panel changes with it and not before. |
111: | F24 | M5 | A wave's spawn queue empties before the next wave is considered, and the next wave begins only when the queue is empty and no enemy remains alive. | Pull the last enemy of a wave out of reach of every tower: no new wave appears while it lives; kill it and the intermission begins. |
112: | F25 | M5 | Wave contents and entry order are authored per stage (Content of record); enemies enter from the field's authored approach directions, weighted toward the recorded distribution. | Clear the same stage twice with the same seed: the same waves arrive in the same order from the same sides. |

Numbers match the core's own arithmetic where that is runnable. |
114: | F27 | M5 | Status effects — burn, slow, stun, poison, invisibility-until-range, resistance — are applied as data with durations authored in seconds (Content of record), expire on their own event, and never carry information a paused game hides. | Slow one enemy with a Cryo Ray and one with Time Slow; read both speeds after the effect ends — back to base, no permanent creep. |
115: | F28 | S2 | Boss stages: the boss arrives as the final wave's climax, flips phase at the recorded HP threshold with its recorded phase behaviour, and a boss threat readout exists only while the boss is live. | Stage 3 at about 50% boss HP: the boss's behaviour visibly changes and its escort arrives; in Stage 1 no such readout ever appears. |
116: | F29 | M1 | Victory = every authored wave cleared with the Command Base alive; defeat = the Command Base destroyed. Both routes land on the results surface, and nothing else ends a stage. | Clear Stage 5 → VICTORY; feed the base → DEFEAT; no other path exits a run. |
117: | F30 | S2 | The five-stage campaign of Content of record is the whole v1 content set, and a stage's own unlock condition is enforced at the hub before entry. | Try to open Stage 4 without clearing Stage 3: blocked, with the reason shown as a keyed string. |
118: 
119: Talents and items.
120: 
121: | # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |
122: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
123: | F31 | S5 | Six active talents (Content of record) at their recorded cost, cooldown and duration; usable only while a run is live; cooldown counted as data, so it survives any presentation being absent. | Fire Meteor twice back to back: refused while cooling, with the remaining time readable even with motion off. |

125: | F33 | S5 | Talent unlock state persists (F36); a locked talent is shown as locked, never silently hidden or falsely offered. | Unlock a talent, leave, return: still unlocked, and a locked one reads as locked rather than missing. |

128: 
129: | # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |
130: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
131: | F34 | S1 | The hub presents the campaign as a readable route: five stages, their cleared state, their earned rating, and what is still locked. | From the hub, a second player can say which stages are done and which is next without being told. |

Nothing in-stage is persisted. | Clear stages, unlock a talent, earn an achievement; close and reopen the map: all four read back, and the starting Mora of a fresh run is unaffected. |
134: | F37 | M4 | The seven achievements (Content of record) are evaluated on their named events, each paying its recorded Mora once and setting its own persisted flag. | Trigger the first-victory achievement: paid once, flagged once, and not paid again on the next win. |

138: Presentation, strings and legibility.
139: 
140: | # | [S] | Requirement | Acceptance — checkable by playing |

143: 
144: ### 6.2 Surfaces
145: 
146: One surface is one screen family the player can be asked to use; a surface is not a module, a folder or a control inventory — no layout is implied here. Each row's waits-on column records which platform fact or open question it depends on, and decides none of them.

148: | # | Surface (EN · CN) | Origin source | What the player does | Acceptance — checkable by playing | Waits on |
149: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
150: | S1 | Campaign Hub · 战役入口 | new construction (the level-select dialogs of `DESIGN_UGC_06_UI_UX.md`; the original's stage-select screen) | Chooses a stage, reads progress, rating, achievements and the talent set. | F34, F30, F38 | A1 (composition), A4 (per-stage entries), A7 (shares the map with the field?) |

312: ## 8. Phasing, exit criteria and the split-map fallback
313: 
314: ### 8.1 Phasing
315: 
316: - Phase 0 — a short investigation. It settles the open questions and builds almost nothing. Measure the open platform questions in writing (one research issue each), run the test procedures in `docs/project/building/phase0-protocols/`, record every measured figure together with the work pass that measured it, and choose one of two routes: a single map, or the split-map fallback. Close the open decisions (D1, D2, D7) to the extent a human will; the platform-free core (the economy code, the tables, the wave scheduler and the random-number generator) is organised and exercised during Phase 0.
317: - Phase 1 — build the surfaces in parallel. One surface per owner, no two owners touching the same files, and nothing published in this phase — a half-built hub is not a map. Order does not matter; the wiring (M1-M7) is integrated last, and the integration owner is responsible for those wiring rows.
318: - Phase 2 — integrate, and publish once. Publication is one event, allowed only when the whole set passes (8.2); the publishing checklist is handed to the human, who alone publishes.
319: 
320: ### 8.2 Whole-set exit criteria
321: 
322: The set a human reads before consenting to publication. Every row is pass/fail by playing; no row may be marked passed on the strength of an agent's own mockup.
323: 
324: 1. Every 6.2 surface row passes its acceptance check and its NFR12 gate on the real map, in both locales.
325: 2. Every 6.3 wiring row passes: one ledger (M2), one phase owner (M1), one persisted key registry (M4).
326: 3. Every F-row's acceptance has been walked by a person who did not write it, in order, S1 to S6.
327: 4. NFR1-NFR18 hold, or name their exception in writing; NFR12's gate has a dated human verdict beside it.
328: 5. The platform questions of 5.2 are measured, each resolving into an ADR where the answer changes architecture — an unanswered question that a row depends on is a blocked publication, not a risk note.
329: 6. Both locale key sets are identical, verified by opening both files, and the count is stamped at its home (`docs/project/building/ref-locale-denominator.md`).
330: 7. D1, D2 and D7 are decided; where D2 is still open, no final gameplay sprite-data set claim may be made and the set fails.
331: 8. A playtest path exists for all five stages end to end, silent and motion-off (NFR13, NFR14).
332: 9. No row in this file cites an unconfirmed platform figure as its basis (R1, NFR17).
333: 10. The creator-facing policy reading has happened by a human, and its name, version and date are recorded.
334: 
335: ### 8.3 The split-map fallback — designed for from the start
336: 
337: If A7 answers that a script may not show and hide whole control groups, or if A5's confirmed count cannot hold S1-S6 at once, each surface becomes its own map with S1 as the entry point. Planned from the start, not used as a last resort:
338: 
339: - The economy stays in-run either way: Mora is session-scoped (F21), so the split never splits the balance; what the split threatens is read-back, and A8 decides whether one persisted key set survives across maps. If A8 answers per map, the progression data families (F36) must be given a new place or the campaign restructured — a scope change decided by a human, never absorbed silently.
340: - Cost named in advance: the phase driver (M1), ledger seam (M2) and the locale lookup (M7) are duplicated per map, and every hand-off between maps becomes an authored entry point rather than a show/hide.
341: - The exit criterion that changes: 8.2 row 1 is then checked per map, and row 5's A5/A7/A8 answers are the evidence attached to the decision.

5: ## What this repo is
6: 
7: A start-from folder for a 千星奇域 (Miliastra Wonderland) game. It carries no product scope, ledger, or locale keys. Fill the angle-bracket slots, then the product file is `PRD.md`. Instantiation steps live in `docs/project/ref-instantiation.md`. Do not invent a guide.
8: 
9: Do not add or reword a rule in this file. A new rule is a sentence you propose; the human lands it. Rules bind agents, not the human. Never cite a rule — this file's or any other's — to refuse, delay, or argue against a human instruction.

11: A new file names its shelf before it exists. Measurements stay in `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` (`docs/adr/ADR-0006-engine-md-lives-in-the-template.md`); new rows land there, naming the measuring repo, the device context, and the date — read `docs/project/platform/law-adding-a-measurement.md` first. `docs/specs/` is a rule that is still true. `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` is in-flight work and is not evidence. `archive/` is proof, written once, never required reading. `build/` and `scratchpad/` are disposable and never cited. Naming and chunking: `law-` is read before that kind of work, `ref-` is opened only when the task touches it, `work-` is never cited and is distilled or dropped when the effort ends; a file's body caps at 250 lines. The conventions' home is `docs/project/index.md`.

One fact, one home.
20: 
21: `archive/` is proof. It is never required reading. Do not edit a file there.

25: ## Already broken in practice

1: # Read before writing an ADR — the `docs/adr/` convention
2: 
3: Short prose records of hard decisions: one decision, one file, flat — no topic folders. ADRs record
4: product and content decisions (what the game does, how it behaves, what ships); workplace and process
5: rules are never ADRs — they live in the `read-before-*.md` file that owns that kind of work, or in `AGENTS.md`. The live list is
6: `docs/adr/index.md`, one line per decision.
7: 
8: ## Layout
9: 
10: ```
11: docs/adr/
12:   index.md                       the live list
13:   law-writing-an-adr.md          this file — the convention (docs/guides/)
14:   ADR-0001-….md … ADR-00NN-….md  one decision per file
15: ```
16: 
17: The index is maintained by hand — there is no generator: adding a decision means adding its `index.md`
18: row in the same change, and if hand maintenance starts to hurt that is a ruling for `AGENTS.md`, never
19: a generator.
20: 
21: ## File anatomy
22: 
23: ```markdown
24: # ADR-0001 — <the decision, stated as a title>
25: 
26: Status: **Accepted** (YYYY-MM-DD — <the human ruling or issue that produced it>)
27: Topic: <1–2 lowercase tags>
28: Law: One sentence stating the decision.
29: 
30: ## Context
31: 
32: ## Decision
33: 
34: ## Consequences
35: ```
36: 
37: | Field | Required | Notes |
38: |---|---|---|
39: | `Status` | yes | `**Accepted** (date — what produced it)`; may wrap onto following lines; retired records get the ARCHIVED banner instead |
40: | `Topic` | yes | 1–2 lowercase tags (`platform`, `layout`, `art`, `localization`, `save`, `rules`, `economy`, `content`) |
41: | `Law` | yes | one sentence; this is the line that appears in `index.md` |
42: | `Supersedes` / `Superseded-by` | no | `ADR-00XX (what was superseded)` — used when only part of a record is replaced |
43: 
44: `Topic:`, `Law:` and `Superseded-by:` go after the whole status value, never inside it. The
45: `index.md` cell copies the record's `Law:` line word for word, plus the one plain cross-reference when
46: the record carries a `Supersedes`/`Superseded-by` line. A changed decision is
47: edited into its record, and the row is rewritten to that record's current `Law:` in the same change —
48: never a dated qualifier, never a silent rewrite.
49: 
50: ## Rules
51: 
52: 1. One decision per file — two decisions means two files.
53: 2. IDs are permanent: global, sequential, four digits from `ADR-0001`, never reused or renumbered.
54: 3. A record states the decision in force: a changed decision is edited in place, and only a
55:    genuinely separate decision is a new ADR carrying `Supersedes: ADR-00XX`. Amendment blocks and
56:    dated changelog entries are never used.
57: 4. ADR before the code — a major architectural decision is recorded before the change goes in.
58: 5. Short: one to two pages; longer means it is really two decisions.
59: 6. Derive the next number by listing `docs/adr/`, never from memory.
60: 7. Name the measurement you are waiting on: a `Law:` that assumes a confirmed figure (a cap, a tick rate,
61:    a budget) is a defect — write what is unmeasured into the record and name the test that will settle it.
62: 8. Cite, do not remember: every factual claim carries a reference relative to the repo root — path and section —
63:    opened at the time of writing.
64: 
65: ## Number allocation
66: 
67: This file is the home of planned ADR numbers. An ADR takes its number when its file is created — the file on
68: disk sets the number, and every planned entry is a suggestion only. A document that expects a future record says which
69: candidate number it is and points here (placeholder `ADR-00NN`); a planned number gives way without complaint to a record
70: already on disk, and after filing you re-point every planned number and name the change in the handover.
71: Permission to start work that an ADR already decided is a ticket question, not a record.
72: 
73: ## Adding a decision
74: 
75: 1. List `docs/adr/` and take the highest existing number + 1.
76: 2. Create `docs/adr/ADR-00NN-<kebab-slug>.md` from the anatomy above.
77: 3. Add its row to `docs/adr/index.md` in the same change — an ADR with no row in the index is not on record.
78: 4. Name it after the issue or plan that motivated it.
79: 
80: ## Superseding and retiring
81: 
82: Supersession is for a separate decision that replaces an older one: add the new ADR with
83: `Supersedes: ADR-00XX` and `Superseded-by: ADR-00ZZ` on the old one, then archive the old record in
84: place, with this notice as its very first line: `> **ARCHIVED (YYYY-MM-DD):** superseded by docs/adr/ADR-00ZZ-….md;
85: kept as historical reference.`
86: 
87: A change to a decision already in force is an edit in place of its own record — no new ADR, nothing
88: appended, no notice, because the ruling is still that record's own. A record whose rules moved out to a
89: workspace file is retired as a supersession, naming that file as the successor. Never `git rm` or
90: delete a tracked doc.

(End of file - total 90 lines)
</content>

7:

33: | ADR-0018 | tooling | The greedy approximation path carries two owner-selectable, default-preserving dials — `budget_currency` (controls \| bytes \| frame), which denominates every rate term the greedy prices, and `lattice_k` (0 \| 1 \| 2), which quantizes generated rect and tri/ring integer coordinates to multiples of 2^k at generation — with defaults `controls` and `0` producing byte-identical output to the pre-dial engine, and the `bytes` table explicitly PROVISIONAL until the real per-kind costs of the payload format (ADR-0016) replace it. |
34: | ADR-0019 | tooling | The product greedy's per-program ceiling on experimental (tri/ring) commits is an owner-selectable, default-preserving dial — `max_experimental_ops` (mixed_ops keyword / CLI `--max-experimental-ops`, any positive int; one shared tri+ring budget, never per-kind; rrect cover ops never experimental and never capped by it) — with default 4 producing byte-identical output to the pre-dial engine, and a recorded-but-unapplied sweep recommendation of 8. |
35: | ADR-0020 | tooling | The working-resolution downscale's interpolation is a dial — `intake_resample`, NEAREST by default (ADR-0008's law stands, byte-identical output) with BOX as the measured opt-in area average (~9–12% fewer ops at unchanged tri adoption on robin) — recorded by absence at the default, owned by the converter's recipe key, and carried into the engine's image front door through that one import, never a second resize rule. |
36: | ADR-0021 | art, tooling | The anim pipeline carries two INDEPENDENT hard ceilings — a stock ceiling `caps_max_controls` bounding live+hidden pooled controls, and flow ceilings `caps_max_creates_per_frame` and `caps_max_mutations_per_frame` (a blunt proxy counting property-sets + retires) — never a combined weighted budget, which would re-introduce the scrapped-λ hidden exchange rate (ADR-0014) and is deferred until a device probe measures per-action costs; enforcement is same-kind slot recycling followed, in order, by create-deferral (debt carried into later frames, round-trip equality once paid) and frame splitting (two half-rate sub-frames at t and t+half), with honest smallest-impact drops after the ladder and static (all-creates) programs failing loudly with dial guidance instead of degrading; runtime hitch defence is a dt-paced content-time clock with CLOCK-SKIP — at most one present per tick, overdue frames skipped, never a queued catch-up burst — plus rolling dt/FPS telemetry, because a static cap cannot DETECT tick overrun; and every dial is default-off and byte-preserving: with all caps unset, emitted payloads and call streams are byte-identical to the uncapped pipeline. |
37: | ADR-0022 | save, tooling | Sequences of frame payloads (clips) may save in a `clip-stream` container — the frame bodies of one per-clip frame dialect (frame-dialect byte `H`, `P`, `K` or `D` — `H`/`P` are standalone payloads chosen per measured size at encode time, while `K` (columnar-book) and `D` (delta-pframes) are not standalone-decodable and are emitted only by their own opt-in builders) carried as segments of raw-DEFLATE (RFC 1951, zlib `wbits=-15`, pinned level 9) with a segment table (frame count and byte length per segment; segment-atomic decode, budgeted stepping), decoded on device by this repo's ORIGINAL inflate written from the public RFC — never a port of third-party decoder code — and chosen INSTEAD of per-frame columnar payloads only for multi-frame clips/animations (a single static image keeps the per-frame dialects of ADR-0016); repeated-shape dedup rides the stream's LZ back-references and NO separate instancing machinery will be built. |
38: | ADR-0023 | art, tooling | The clip payload's frame-record grammar gains two opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving compression record modes — the implicit base-color frame (when a frame's painting is majority one colour, the record carries that base colour once and emits ONLY non-base ops; painting treats unpainted cells as the base for that frame, the reference's mode-1 idiom) and the hold-frame token (a 1-byte "repeat last frame" record for identical consecutive frames whose runtime apply is a no-op) — with the encoder declining (emitting the ordinary record) whenever the mode does not verify or does not save bytes; with both dials off, every emitted stream is byte-identical to the pre-extension pipeline, pinned against the committed fixtures. |
39: | ADR-0024 | save, platform | Every Lua file on the shipping surface (`platform-free-core/**/*.lua`, payload_format.lua primarily) is written to the Lua 5.3 grammar and stdlib only — no 5.4-only construct (`<const>`/`<close>` attributes, `warn`, `coroutine.close`, 5.4 lexical scoping) may ride into the device player — while the dev-side interpreters and gates stay on the local Lua 5.4 (a strict superset for this codebase), so both versions run the same self-checks green. |
40: | ADR-0025 | art, tooling | The anim P-frame grammar gains two opt-in, default-off, byte-preserving whole-frame transform records — the camera-pan `pan(dx, dy, covered)` (one record instead of the N position property-sets of every conforming matched control) and the palette-permutation `permute(table)` (one moved-entries table instead of N colour-sets) — detected at encode time by threshold-gated pattern recognition over the native diff stream, verified per frame against the frame program with the engine's own composite, and a RUNTIME HONESTY LAW: absent the ISSUE-009 probe 11 container-parenting result, the runtime applies both records by LOOP — N property-sets, not one — so every byte/churn saving is reported alongside the unchanged (or honestly worse) expanded runtime call count, and the flow-cap accounting (ADR-0021) counts EXPANDED sets, never record count. |

1: # ADR-0006 — The gate condition is retired: two decisions shed it, their rules stand
2: 
3: Status: **Accepted** (2026-10-02 — human ruling. The "phase gate" these records were conditioned on was found to be
4: agent-authored template boilerplate carried in from a sibling template repo with no human ratification, and the human
5: has ruled it void: it forbade the module tree, scene tree and control inventory this project needs, and it reserved
6: the nine platform questions to a closure no agent could perform. The two conditioned decisions are superseded **in
7: part** — the gate clause dies, the decision stands unweakened. Measured platform facts and the open questions now
8: live in `docs/specs/platform-facts.md`.)
9: Supersedes: `ADR-0002` (the "§ *Phase gate* withholds layout" statement) · `ADR-0004` (the "no agent may close the
10: in-editor checks" clause) · `ADR-0005` (the "Source code remains outside this change while the phase gate is open"
11: clause), each **in part**, by `docs/adr/read-before-writing-an-adr.md` § *Superseding and retiring*.
12: Topic: platform, layout
13: 
14: ## Law
15: 
16: The two decisions that were written conditioned on the phase gate — the platform-free core carve-out (`ADR-0002`) and
17: the art-loads-in-source / code-owned-sprites pair (`ADR-0004`, `ADR-0005`) — stand **on their own ground**. Their
18: conditioning clauses are withdrawn: layout is not "withheld", the in-editor checks are not "closed by no agent", and
19: source code is not "outside this change while the gate is open". What remains in force is what each decision actually
20: argued: the core is Lua naming no platform call, control, save-variable runtime form, coordinate or cap, organised per
21: surface and per shared concern, run under this machine's interpreter as a development tool and never a payload
22: dependency; art is loaded into the map as editor image assets and never drawn at runtime; gameplay sprites enter code
23: as data and render through client controls. The nine platform questions stay open as **questions** in
24: `docs/specs/platform-facts.md` — measurements nobody has taken — and nothing reserves their answering to a human or
25: forbids an agent to record a measured answer; an answer lands where it is measured.
26: 
27: ## Context
28: 
29: - The rule this record retires was never a human's. It entered as template boilerplate from a sibling template repo
30:   and was propagated into this repo's `AGENTS.md` / `PRD.md` / `CONTEXT.md` framing without ratification; the human has
31:   ruled it void and the repo's rule pages no longer carry it. A decision conditioned on a void condition keeps its
32:   decision and loses the condition.
33: - Each of the three records already argued its own case independent of the gate: `ADR-0002` rests on the platform
34:   giving a script no libraries, no build step and no filesystem, and on its 5.1-safe subset being enforced by a static
35:   gate module — a dev tool, not the retired rule; `ADR-0004` rests on art costing a budget rather than code;
36:   `ADR-0005` rests on there being no external gameplay image upload/import path.
37: - The questions the gate named are real and still unanswered. They are measurements, not a licence an agent was
38:   forbidden to use.
39: 
40: ## Decision
41: 
42: - **`ADR-0002` — the carve-out stands; the withholding statement is cut.** "`AGENTS.md` § *Phase gate* withholds …
43:   layout" is withdrawn. The core claims no layout because it is a pure-rule module, not because anything withholds one;
44:   the layout question is an open platform question in `docs/specs/platform-facts.md`. The core's 5.1-safe subset stays
45:   enforced by the static gate module named in that record — that gate is a linter, unrelated to the retired rule, and
46:   is untouched by this supersession.
47: - **`ADR-0004` — the art ruling stands; the closure clause is cut.** "in-editor checks no agent may close" is
48:   withdrawn; the checks are open measurements, not a reserved closure.
49: - **`ADR-0005` — the code-owned-sprites ruling stands; its duration clause is cut.** "Source code remains outside this
50:   change while the phase gate is open" is withdrawn.
51: - **No rule is weakened and none is strengthened.** This record removes a condition; it changes no decision's
52:   substance. Where a conditioned record said "X, while the gate is open", it now says "X".
53: 
54: ## Consequences
55: 
56: - The three records gain an appended `Superseded-by: ADR-0006` line naming the clause cut — **no archive banner**, per
57:   the partial-supersede carve-out; their bodies are otherwise unedited and their own words stand as written.
58: - Their index rows state the record's current `Law:` line plus one plain cross-reference to this record; the `Law` cells are not silently rewritten.
59: - `docs/specs/platform-facts.md` is the single home of the measured facts and the open questions.
60: - No A1–A9 question is answered by this record — the questions are open and unanswered; this record only removes the
61:   claim that an agent was forbidden to answer them.

(End of file - total 61 lines)
</content>

1: # ADR-0005 — code-owned gameplay sprites rendered through client controls
2: 
3: Status: **Accepted** (2026-09-30 — human product ruling, tracked by ISSUE-052)
4: Topic: art, platform
5: Law: Gameplay sprites enter code as data and render through client controls with no external gameplay image upload/import path; cover imagery is outside gameplay, and the data/control budget remains an open A5/A9 human gate.
6: Supersedes: ADR-0004 (gameplay sprite ingress and rendering route only)
7: Superseded-by: `ADR-0006` (2026-10-02) — **in part:** the *Decision* clause "Source code remains outside this change while the phase gate is open" is withdrawn (the gate it named is void); the code-owned-sprites ruling stands unweakened.
8: 
9: ## Context
10: 
11: ADR-0004 made editor image assets the gameplay art route, required the map to ingest those assets, and rejected runtime data-to-control rendering as a shipping shape (`docs/adr/ADR-0004-art-loads-in-source-undecided.md` § *Decision*, clauses 1–4). The living product language repeated that route: `AGENTS.md` § *What this project is* and § *Stack and platform*, `CONTEXT.md` § *Platform* and `PRD.md` § *Non-goals*, § *Platform constraints*, § *Posture rows N1-N5*, and § *Open decisions D1, D2, D3, D7*.
12: 
13: The A9 protocol and its owning ticket consequently ask a human to measure external image pickers, imported image files, image IDs and image-count or byte ceilings (`docs/specs/phase0-protocols/a9-sprite-budget.md` § *The ladder, numbered*; `issue-tracker/open/ISSUE-009-open-a9-sprite-budget-probe.md` § *The exact in-editor check*). Those are not the gameplay route under the current ruling. A5 still owns client-control capacity, and A9 still owns the sprite-budget gate, but neither gate has been answered by this record.
14: 
15: Cover imagery is not gameplay presentation. It is outside this decision and must not be used as evidence for, or as a substitute for, the gameplay sprite route.
16: 
17: ## Decision
18: 
19: 1. **Gameplay sprite ingress is code-owned data.** Gameplay sprite identities, palette or colour data, dimensions, frames and other representation data enter the code-owned data path. No gameplay sprite enters through an external image upload or import path, and no gameplay asset tree is implied by this record.
20: 2. **Gameplay sprite presentation is control-owned.** Client controls render the code-owned sprite data for gameplay. The control representation, count, layout and any pooling remain unchosen until the human gates answer; this record does not create a source layout or turn a cap into a constant.
21: 3. **The previous route is superseded only where it conflicts.** ADR-0004 remains an immutable record of its earlier ruling. Its gameplay image-asset ingress, no-runtime-draw route and blanket rejection of the data-to-control rect-explosion shape are superseded by this record; its historical measurements and its warnings not to invent A5/A9 figures remain historical context, not current gameplay law.
22: 4. **Cover imagery is out of scope.** A cover image is not a gameplay sprite, does not establish a gameplay upload/import path, and does not enter the A5/A9 gameplay measurement as a substitute for the sprite-data route.
23: 5. **A5 and A9 remain human gates.** A5 must still establish the client-control capacity and counting rule. A9 must still establish the capacity and constraints that matter to code-owned sprite data rendered through those controls. No number, dimension, format, control count or other platform cap is confirmed here, and no gate is closed by this ADR.
24: 
25: ## Consequences
26: 
27: - The current law docs must describe code-owned gameplay sprite data and client-control rendering, not editor image assets, image IDs or gameplay upload/import.
28: - ISSUE-009 and the A9 protocol must replace image-picker and imported-file measurements with the code-data/control measurements that A9 still needs. Any unresolved editor observation remains a human gate.
29: - No gameplay sprite source set, data table, control inventory, scene layout or implementation is created by this ADR.
30: - The old ADR is not rewritten. Readers use this later accepted ADR for the current gameplay route and retain ADR-0004 for its historical record and non-conflicting context.

(End of file - total 30 lines)
</content>

55:    genuinely separate decision is a new ADR carrying `Supersedes: ADR-00XX`. Amendment blocks and
56:    dated changelog entries are never used.
57: 4. ADR before the code — a major architectural decision is recorded before the change goes in.
58: 5. Short: one to two pages; longer means it is really two decisions.
59: 6. Derive the next number by listing `docs/adr/`, never from memory.
60: 7. Name the measurement you are waiting on: a `Law:` that assumes a confirmed figure (a cap, a tick rate,
61:    a budget) is a defect — write what is unmeasured into the record and name the test that will settle it.
62: 8. Cite, do not remember: every factual claim carries a reference relative to the repo root — path and section —
63:    opened at the time of writing.
64: 
65: ## Number allocation
66: 
67: This file is the home of planned ADR numbers. An ADR takes its number when its file is created — the file on
68: disk sets the number, and every planned entry is a suggestion only. A document that expects a future record says which
69: candidate number it is and points here (placeholder `ADR-00NN`); a planned number gives way without complaint to a record
70: already on disk, and after filing you re-point every planned number and name the change in the handover.
71: Permission to start work that an ADR already decided is a ticket question, not a record.
72: 
73: ## Adding a decision
74: 
75: 1. List `docs/adr/` and take the highest existing number + 1.
76: 2. Create `docs/adr/ADR-00NN-<kebab-slug>.md` from the anatomy above.
77: 3. Add its row to `docs/adr/index.md` in the same change — an ADR with no row in the index is not on record.
78: 4. Name it after the issue or plan that motivated it.
79: 
80: ## Superseding and retiring
81: 
82: Supersession is for a separate decision that replaces an older one: add the new ADR with
83: `Supersedes: ADR-00XX` and `Superseded-by: ADR-00ZZ` on the old one, then archive the old record in
84: place, with this notice as its very first line: `> **ARCHIVED (YYYY-MM-DD):** superseded by docs/adr/ADR-00ZZ-….md;
85: kept as historical reference.`
86: 
87: A change to a decision already in force is an edit in place of its own record — no new ADR, nothing
88: appended, no notice, because the ruling is still that record's own. A record whose rules moved out to a
89: workspace file is retired as a supersession, naming that file as the successor. Never `git rm` or
90: delete a tracked doc.

(End of file - total 90 lines)

## Product

娣辩┖椹诲煄 (Taskworld Project) re-expresses the Flash tower-defense Enigmata: Stellar War as a 鍗冩槦濂囧煙 map 鈥?free placement of defensive structures, timed enemy waves, boss stages, one Mora ledger 鈥?driven by Lua client scripts over editor-authored client controls. EN Taskworld Project, CN 娣辩┖椹诲煄; `Taskworld-Project` is the repo name only. Surfaces S1鈥揝6 and wiring M1鈥揗7 are registered in `PRD.md`. The shipping target is everything; a map per surface is designed from the start.

The source set `other games reference material/enigmata-stellar-war/` is read-only and not a compatibility target. Mechanics and content are re-typed in Lua. No file of code, audio, font or string carries over. Gameplay sprites are code-owned data rendered through client controls (`docs/adr/ADR-0005-code-owned-gameplay-sprites.md`). Cover imagery is outside gameplay.

## Stack

Genshin Impact 鍗冩槦濂囧煙 UGC; the editor is 鍗冩槦娌欑, PC-only (`PRD.md` 搂 Platform constraints). No engine, package manager, test harness, filesystem, or build step in what ships. Payload scripts `require` only and read and write no file; persistence is cloud-save variables only.

Write Lua 5.3, nothing environment-adjacent. A construct only newer Lua accepts is not an all-clear. Dialect probe: `ISSUE-014`. The runtime supplies no libraries, no LuaJIT, no `load`/`loadstring`. Missing facilities are rewritten in portable Lua.

`platform-free-core/` is the one carve-out (`docs/adr/ADR-0002-platform-free-core-and-carve-out.md`): pure Lua naming no platform call, run under this machine's `lua.exe` as a development tool, never a payload dependency. Module law: `platform-free-core/README.md`. The 5.1-safe subset is policed by `dev/lua-gate/`, not by that interpreter 鈥?local Lua 5.4.5 parses what the subset bans (`docs/project/building/ref-lua-subset-gate.md`). A local named exactly `oddx` miscompiles; rename and re-run before believing the failure. A green local run is arithmetic evidence only, never proof the payload loads.

A documented figure is never a designable number. Engine measurements live in `../miliastra-game-template/docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md`. A number copied into this repo is stale. Design against a value you confirmed in the editor, and expect it to move.

1: # project — the project documentation index
2: 
3: Always read this index on entering `docs/project/`. It is the routing table for this repo; there is no other index beside it.
4: 
5: ## Routing
6: 
7: | Kind of thing | Home |
8: | --- | --- |
9: | A measured platform fact | one row in the template's measurement table, `C:\Users\AAAAA\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\docs\project\platform\ref-measurements.md` (device 2: the same path under `C:\Users\TZ\Desktop\miliastra-game-template\`) |

12: | Operating the editor or the game | `docs/project/sessions/` |
13: | A rule for working on this repo | `docs/guides/` |
14: | A product or content decision | `docs/adr/` |
15: | In-flight work | `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` until it is settled and moved to its permanent home |
16: | A raw record | `archive/` — written once, never required reading |
17: 
18: ## Naming and size
19: 
20: Three prefixes, on files and on index lines. `law-` is binding: read it before doing the kind of work the filename names. `ref-` is reference: open it only when the task touches the named topic, and it is the default for project knowledge. `work-` is in-flight notes for one effort: no `law-` or `ref-` file ever cites it, and it is settled into a permanent file or moved to `archive/` when the effort ends. This file is where these conventions are stated.
21: 
22: Each document covers one topic, stands alone, and opens with one scope line naming its section. Its body is capped at 150 lines; past that it splits by topic, never by part number, and the split updates this index in the same change. Each fact has exactly one home; other documents link to it instead of repeating it. English and its Chinese counterpart stay inside the same topic document.
23: 
24: ### Where this repo departs from the template's conventions
25: 
26: The template's `docs/project/index.md` states a 250-line body cap, names a "chunk" rather than a document, and routes "a rule that is still true" to its own `docs/specs/` shelf. 1: # project — the project documentation index
2: 
3: Always read this index on entering `docs/project/`. It is the routing table for this repo; there is no other index beside it.
4: 
5: ## Routing
6: 
7: | Kind of thing | Home |
8: | --- | --- |
9: | A measured platform fact | one row in the template checkout's measurement table — `docs/project/platform/ref-measurements.md` inside the `miliastra-game-template` folder on either device's Desktop |
10: | How to build | `docs/project/building/` |
11: | A rule that is still true | `docs/guides/` (a `law-` file) or `docs/project/` (a `ref-` file) |
12: | Operating the editor or the game | `docs/project/sessions/` |
13: | A rule for working on this repo | `docs/guides/` |
14: | A product or content decision | `docs/adr/` |
15: | In-flight work | `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>/` until it is settled and moved to its permanent home |
16: | A raw record | `archive/` — written once, never required reading |
17: 
18: ## Naming and size
19: 
20: Three prefixes, on files and on index lines. `law-` is binding: read it before doing the kind of work the filename names. `ref-` is reference: open it only when the task touches the named topic, and it is the default for project knowledge. `work-` is in-flight notes for one effort: no `law-` or `ref-` file ever cites it, and it is settled into a permanent file or moved to `archive/` when the effort ends. This file is where these conventions are stated.
21: 
22: Each document covers one topic, stands alone, and opens with one scope line naming its section. Its body is capped at 150 lines; past that it splits by topic, never by part number, and the split updates this index in the same change. Each fact has exactly one home; other documents link to it instead of repeating it. English and its Chinese counterpart stay inside the same topic document.
23: 
24: ### Where this repo departs from the template's conventions
25: 
26: The template's `docs/project/index.md` states a 250-line body cap, names a "chunk" rather than a document, and routes "a rule that is still true" to its own `docs/specs/` shelf. This repo keeps its own older convention on the first two and has no `docs/specs/` shelf, so the third cannot be adopted as written. The decision, so a reader does not have to guess:
27: 
28: - **Body cap: 150 lines, this repo's rule wins.** No in-scope file approaches either figure today, so nothing has to be split by this choice; a future split follows 150 and updates this index in the same change.
29: - **Vocabulary: "document", not "chunk".** The template's word is not imported; every other in-scope file already says document or file.
30: - **Rules that are still true: no `docs/specs/` shelf here.** The template has one at `docs/specs/` inside its own checkout; this repo never had one and creates none. A rule that is still true lands in a `law-` file in `docs/guides/` when it governs a procedure, or in a `ref-` file in `docs/project/` when it states a project fact. The template's `docs/specs/` is reference only and is not this repo's shelf.
31: 
32: ## This directory
33: 
34: - `ref-glossary.md` — pointer to the glossary and path index kept at the repo root, `CONTEXT.md`. Open when a task needs a term's definition, the Avoid list, or the path index.
35: - `ref-official-docs.md` — pointer to the mirrored official corpus. Open when a task needs the mirrored official 千星奇域 corpus.
36: 
37: Both files are in this directory. Neither holds content; each names the shelf that does.
38: 
39: ## Sections
40: 
41: - `platform/index.md` — measured platform behavior and this repo's open platform questions. Open when a task needs a measured platform number or an open platform question.
42: - `building/index.md` — how this game is built. Open when a task reads or changes the build of the game.
43: - `sessions/index.md` — operating the editor and the game. Open when a task drives the editor or the game.
44: - `docs/guides/index.md` — procedures for working on this repo. Read before the kind of work a guide names.

(End of file - total 44 lines)
</content>
